sources.citation: Ethnologue, 18th ed. (2015), entry 'Malapandaram' [mjp] (the Internet Archive 2016 copy)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Dialects: None known. Lexical similarity: 83%-94% between varieties in Kerala, 63%-68% with Malayalam [mal], 64%-68% with Tamil'; classification Dravidian > Southern > Tamil-Kannada > Tamil-Kodagu > Tamil-Malayalam > Malayalam; 'Language Use: Shift toward Malayalam'.

sources.citation: Varghese, Bijumon & Jose P. Mathew. 2015. Tribes of Idukki, Kerala. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2015-029. Dallas: SIL International. iii+186 pp. (fieldwork 2001-02; the only OLAC-listed resource for mjp)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.10 (p. 11): 'They speak a dialect of Malayalam, locally termed Pandaram Bhasha' (citing Singh 1994:733; Luiz in Menon 1996:212: 'speak a poor dialect with many Tamil and Malayalam words and phrases'). Sec. 7.3.5 (p. 45): 'No language information was collected from the Mala Pandaram families that live in Idukki district'; recommends a survey in Kollam/Pathanamthitta. No wordlist, no phonology.

sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13:7 (July 2013), 58 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Malapandaram sketch at all; the language is named once (Malaveda section: Malavedas 'are considered to be closely related to Ulladans and Malappandarams'). Sketches cover Adiya, Aranadan, Cholanaikkan, Irula, Kani, Kurichiya, Kurumba, Malamuthan, Malaveda, Mannan, Muduga etc. No stress statement for Malapandaram.
